definition: RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX VSR) is a video scaling feature by Nvidia.

explainer.lead: RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX VSR) is Nvidia's video scaling feature, released on February 28, 2023. It matters because it upscales video in real time, improving playback quality without a separate high-resolution source.

tiers.eli5: It's like a magnifying glass for video that sharpens the picture as it plays instead of just making it bigger and blurrier.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers enable it in the graphics pipeline to upscale streamed or low-resolution video on the fly. A common pitfall is that upscaled detail is synthesized, so it can look wrong on content with fine textures or text.
tiers.paperLevel: A video scaling feature by Nvidia, released February 28, 2023; as a super-resolution method it infers high-resolution output from lower-resolution input, so it cannot recover detail absent from the source.

explainer.example: A 1080p stream is upscaled to 4K in real time on a supported Nvidia GPU during playback.
